summary: LS Power Grid California files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in ER27-528-000, answering the CAISO show cause order. It adds a large load interconnection process and a pro forma cost recovery agreement with a 20-year minimum revenue contribution. The letter matches the DesertLink filing in ER27-534; the differences are in the Formula Rate Template and the project descriptions.
ask: Accept the revisions effective January 16, 2027, 61 days after filing, and grant any waivers needed.

points.point: It adds a process for utilities that buy transmission service on behalf of large loads.
points.quote: adding a new Section 10A and a new Appendix VI (Large Load Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”)) to establish an interconnection process for Eligible Customers for Large Load (“ECLLs”)

points.point: The definition is 50 MW of peak load at a single site.
points.quote: a Large Load is an End-User located at a single site behind one or more Points of Withdrawal from the CAISO Controlled Grid with a peak load of 50 MW or greater

points.point: The cost recovery agreement sets a 20-year minimum revenue contribution for each upgrade.
points.quote: establishes the Eligible Customer’s twenty-year Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“MTRC”) and related payment and security obligations for each Covered Upgrade

points.point: Ending service early costs the customer all remaining revenue responsibility.
points.quote: the Eligible Customer owes a lump-sum Termination Fee equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility

points.point: Direct security can be reduced by security the large load posted under a retail agreement.
points.quote: allowing an Eligible Customer to rely on credit support posted by a large load under a retail agreement, direct Operational Security is reduced dollar-for-dollar by Qualifying Retail Security Support

points.point: Interim curtailable service is curtailed ahead of firm service.
points.quote: FILI Service is subject to curtailment, including during normal operating conditions, and is curtailed before Firm Interconnection Service

points.point: LS Power Grid has no retail customers and no retail relationship with a large load.
points.quote: LS Power Grid is a non-load-serving PTO with no End-Use Customers; it neither serves retail load nor has a retail relationship with any customer seeking a Large Load interconnection

points.point: This is the difference from DesertLink: LS Power Grid says its formula rate template needs no changes.
points.quote: requires no changes to LS Power Grid’s Formula Rate Template or Protocols

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-10 show cause order. It adds a large load interconnection process and a pro forma cost recovery agreement to a transmission-only owner's tariff, and defers permanent flexible service to CAISO.
